title: Machine learning prediction of PFAS removal performance in electrospun nanofiber filtration systems
content: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent water contaminants that pose significant environmental and health concerns. Electrospun nanofibers have emerged as a promising platform for PFAS removal owing to their high surface area and tunable surface functionalities. However, experimental optimization of nanofiber design and operating conditions is costly and time-intensive. In this study, machine learning (ML) regression models were leveraged to predict PFAS removal efficiency using a literature-derived dataset comprising 326 experimental observations from 21 independent studies. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this study presents the first supervised ML framework leveraged for predicting PFAS removal efficiency in electrospun nanofiber systems. Uniquely, we incorporate categorical descriptors, including polymer type, surface modification type, and PFAS functional group, which have not been systematically encoded as features in previous PFAS adsorption ML models. To assess the influence of validation strategy on model performance, conventional five-fold row-wise cross-validation was compared with study-grouped nested cross-validation using the same development dataset. Conventional row-wise validation yielded an out-of-fold (OOF) R2 of 0.684, MAE of 12.74%, and RMSE of 19.73% for CatBoost. In contrast, nested study-grouped validation produced R2 = 0.373, MAE = 23.49%, and RMSE = 27.79%. Following final grouped hyperparameter tuning, CatBoost achieved a grouped OOF R2 of 0.456, MAE of 21.77%, and RMSE of 25.88%. The final study-grouped CatBoost model was evaluated on 65 observations from five completely unseen studies, achieving an external R2 of 0.744, MAE of 9.92%, and RMSE of 13.99%. Feature importance and SHAP analyses revealed that surface modification class, PFAS chain class, and fiber diameter were consistently among the most influential model predictors. These findings highlight the importance of study-aware validation when evaluating ML models trained on literature-derived experimental datasets and demonstrate the potential of ML for screening electrospun nanofiber systems for PFAS removal.
